question: is the per-frame drift global gain, pixel noise, or a spatial change in the scene?
correction: An earlier report said per-frame gain normalisation cut drift from 43.3 to 0.81 counts. It did not: it compared raw counts against relative units. 43.686/111.18 = 0.393 and 43.226/109.71 = 0.394, so the reduction was 1.00x, not ~50x. That error is why gain_invariance.py could not work.

captures.label: OCCUPIED (facing, speaking)
captures.classification: SPATIAL STRUCTURE, not noise: the residual survives 2x2 averaging (ratio 0.97, pure noise would be 0.50) and gain explains only 2.8%

captures.label: EMPTY (nobody, dark room)
captures.classification: SPATIAL STRUCTURE, not noise: the residual survives 2x2 averaging (ratio 1.00, pure noise would be 0.50) and gain explains only 4.3%

method: least-squares fit of one scalar k per adjacent frame pair through the origin; residual is what a global gain cannot explain. Noise test: RMS of the residual after 2x2 block averaging, relative to before -- pure independent noise gives ~0.50, structure survives.
verdict: Gain explains 4.3% of the drift in EMPTY (nobody, dark room), and the residual noise ratio is 1.00. SPATIAL STRUCTURE, not noise: the residual survives 2x2 averaging (ratio 1.00, pure noise would be 0.50) and gain explains only 4.3%
